Why some filters are marked *

A single grant can sit in more than one region, category or type, so two filters can hand you the same call twice. The pairs below overlap enough to be worth flagging, and every filter involved carries an asterisk above.

Categories

  • Cross-disciplinary & Social Impact and Media Arts, Film & Sound — 52 shared
Open feed
How to subscribe (RSS reader or email)
  1. Optionally tick one or more Categories and pick a Region and Type to narrow the feed. Every feed releases weekly: the week's new grants arrive together on Sunday, one entry per grant plus a short roundup header.
  2. Ticking several options gives you one feed URL each. Design plus Game Design is two URLs; two categories across three regions is six. Copy URL grabs them all at once. Subscribe to the lot and put them in one folder in your reader — Feedly, Inoreader and NetNewsWire all show a folder as a single merged stream.
  3. Duplicates when you subscribe to two feeds. Every grant carries the same permanent id in every feed it appears in, so any reader with a duplicate filter (Inoreader has one built in) collapses it to a single entry automatically. Readers without one show it twice. The only way to guarantee no duplicates is to use a single feed that already covers what you want, so if you keep pairing the same two boxes, ask for them to be merged into one option — that is exactly what "AI, Tech, Digital Infrastructure" and "Media Arts & Film" already are.
  4. Why not one URL for any union? Every feed here is a pre-built file, and one file per possible combination of ticks would run to tens of thousands.
  5. Timeline stands on its own. The deadline windows cover every region, category and type, so picking one clears the others. Combining them was dropped: it quadrupled the number of feeds, and "closing in the next 30 days" is a question this website answers better than a feed reader can.
  6. Some Type combinations have no grants yet (there may be no curator prizes in LatAm this month). Those feeds are not generated, and the picker tells you rather than handing you a dead link.
  7. Copy the feed URL above (or click Open feed to preview it).
  8. Paste the URL into either:
    • An RSS reader — Feedly, NetNewsWire, Inoreader, Reeder, Thunderbird. New entries appear in the reader as they're added.
    • A free RSS-to-email service for an inbox digest, no account needed here:
      • Kill the Newsletter — dead simple, no signup; generates a unique address that turns each new feed item into a plain email.
      • Blogtrottr — pick realtime, daily or weekly digest.
      • Feedrabbit — similar digest controls, free up to a few feeds.
  9. Cadence changes how much lands in your reader, not how often it checks (RSS readers poll on their own schedule, which the site cannot set). One entry per grant is the original feed: new calls arrive in a steady trickle, roughly five a day. Weekly digest collapses the same grants into a single entry per week listing everything released that week, so you get one item instead of about thirty-five. Pair the digest with an RSS-to-email bridge below and it becomes one email a week.
  10. Deadline-filtered feeds (Next 30 / 90 days) only include grants with a fixed deadline in that window. Rolling/undated grants are excluded from those.
  11. "Added in last 30 days" includes everything added recently regardless of deadline (great for a "what's new" feed and the closest match to a newsletter when paired with a weekly email digest).

Add deadlines to your calendar

A live calendar of upcoming deadlines. Stays in sync as new calls land or details change.

Rolling and undated calls never appear here, because a calendar entry needs a date. Recently closed deadlines stay visible for 60 days. Subscribing to several calendars can show the same call once per calendar.

How to subscribe
  1. Optionally tick one or more Categories and/or pick a Region to narrow the calendar. If you tick multiple categories, you'll get one .ics URL per category, which you can subscribe to separately.
  2. Copy the calendar URL.
  3. Google Calendar: "Other calendars" → "+" → "From URL", paste, Add.
  4. Apple Calendar: "File" → "New Calendar Subscription", paste, OK.
  5. Outlook: "Add calendar" → "Subscribe from web", paste.
  6. Your calendar refreshes every few hours, so new grants and changes flow in automatically.

Grants, Fellowships and Residencies in AI, Arts, Film, Journalism, Research and Tech The Grant Desk

-- active grants on the desk right now. The Grant Desk is a free tool. No account, paywall or subscription required. The site consists of a hand-picked selection of paid open calls, fellowships and residencies for artists, journalists, writers, researchers and technologists working in the realm of digital media, AI, and technology and society, with a few notable unpaid open calls and festival submissions included as clearly flagged exceptions. Star a card to save it to a shortlist you can share as a link or download as an .ics calendar, and use the "Copy info" button on any card to copy the full grant details to your clipboard. The desk also remembers when you last visited (saved in your browser's localStorage only, not on any server) so the "Show only new" filter highlights what has been added since.

Subscribe via RSS or add deadlines to your calendar so you do not miss a thing.

Format
Detail

Markdown is the best default for pasting into an LLM: one heading per opportunity, labelled fields, and a header noting which filters were applied. Use JSON if you want the model to sort, score or re-rank entries programmatically, and CSV for a spreadsheet. Summary only trims each description to its opening paragraph, which keeps a large export inside a smaller context window. Everything is generated in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

All caught up. Nothing new since your last visit. Show only new filters the page to grants added since your last visit. Mark as seen clears the NEW badges and banner. Your history is saved only in this browser on this device, so it will not transfer to other devices or other browsers, and it gets erased if you clear your cookies or site data.

Watch for next round

Funders whose current cycle is closed but whose next call is expected. Not counted in the active grants tally. Entries are auto-removed once their expected window has passed; check the funder page directly for confirmed dates.

  • Africa No Filter: Last Mile Film Fund (Africa and diaspora) . Checked 24 August 2026: the page is marked Closed and still describes the 2024 cycle, so there is nothing to apply to. When it reopens it pays up to USD 10,000 for feature-length films and up to USD 5,000 for shorts, aimed squarely at final-stage production and post-production (editing, VFX, sound mixing, dubbing, marketing, distribution) for fiction, documentary and animation. Films must be African-led, submitted in their original language with English or French subtitles if needed, and ready to complete and premiere within a year of contracting. Projects still in development or production are not eligible. Applicants must first join ANF's African Narrative Collective, which is worth doing in advance since only members can apply.
  • Africa No Filter: Work Reimagined StoryLab (Africa and diaspora) . Checked 24 August 2026: the last cycle closed 30 April 2025 and the page has not been refreshed since, so watch for a 2026 or 2027 round. Run with the Ford Foundation, it pays micro-grants of up to USD 3,500 to journalists, podcasters and content creators reporting on the future of work in Africa (outsourcing, remote and gig work, low wages, job insecurity, exploitation by international corporations), plus mentorship, exclusive data on Africa's future of work, and publishing opportunities with major outlets. Open to content creators and podcasters aged 18 or over with at least 2,000 combined followers, and to junior, mid-career and freelance journalists in Africa and the diaspora.
  • Creative Europe Culture strand (EU and associated countries) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: all 2026 Culture calls have closed. European Cooperation Projects, the flagship call with a EUR 60 million budget supporting around 150 projects, closed 5 May 2026; it runs two tiers, small scale needing a minimum of three partners for up to EUR 200,000 and medium scale needing five partners for up to EUR 1 million. Circulation of European Literary Works, EUR 5 million for around 40 translation and publishing projects covering at least five works of fiction each, closed 29 January 2026. The 2027 calls are normally published in the last quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, so re-check from November. Open to organisations across all cultural and creative sectors, though projects that are exclusively audiovisual, or made up only of audiovisual-sector organisations, are excluded. Dutch applicants can get free help from the Creative Europe Desk NL.
  • Prix Ars Electronica (Linz, Austria) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the 2026 round has closed and the next open call launches in January 2027, so re-check from then. The longest-running media arts prize: a Golden Nica in each category carries EUR 10,000 in prize money, while Awards of Distinction and Honorary Mentions carry recognition but no cash. Recent categories were New Animation Art, Artificial Life and Intelligence, Digital Musics and Sound Art, and u19 create your world. Winners are presented at the Ars Electronica Festival in Linz. Open internationally.
  • S+T+ARTS Prize (European Commission, administered by Ars Electronica) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the 2026 round ran 7 January to 9 March 2026 and has closed; expect the 2027 call to open around January, so re-check from then. Two prizes of EUR 20,000 each, awarded for innovation at the intersection of science, technology and the arts: one for artistic exploration and one for innovative collaboration between the arts and industry or science. Open internationally.
  • iMAL Fellowship Programme (Brussels, Belgium) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the 2026 call closed 19 April 2026 and no 2027 call is posted yet; the programme has run annually with a spring deadline, so re-check from March. Up to eight weeks in Brussels with a budget of EUR 8,000, split as EUR 4,000 fee and EUR 4,000 for project production, plus accommodation, a workspace and access to iMAL's infrastructure. For artists working with digital and media practices.
  • Rijksakademie Residency 2028 (Amsterdam, Netherlands) . The open call for the 2028 residency opens 1 January 2027, so re-check from then. A two-year residency for international visual artists with a stipend of EUR 19,800 paid in monthly instalments, a private studio, extensive technical facilities, a library and collections, a social practice workshop, and a working budget of EUR 2,500 a year from the Rijksakademie Artists Endowment Fund and Stichting Ammodo. CAVEATS against the desk's funded-only bar: there is a non-refundable application fee of EUR 60, waived for artists living in countries on the OECD DAC list, and a participation fee of EUR 1,875 per year payable by every resident before each residency year starts. Figures are the 2026 ones and may change for 2028.
  • EDSAFE AI Fellowships 2027 (online, US-centred) . Applications for the 2026 cohort are closed; the official page states that applications for 2027 reopen in November 2026, with fellows announced the following January, so re-check from November. The last cycle closed 30 November 2025. Three pathways: Catalyst, for education-sector leaders from industry and the field; Women in AI, for women technologists and educational leaders; and Vanguard, added in 2026, for leaders from K-12, state and local education agencies working on AI policy and best practice. Roughly a 12-month part-time commitment in cohorts of 30-plus, with interactive virtual workshops led by AI experts, learning around emerging trends and the SAFE framework, mentorship from previous fellows, and at least one in-person gathering a year; the emphasis is on applying the learning to real challenges in education. IMPORTANT: EDSAFE publishes no stipend figure and does not state whether the fellowship is paid or whether fellows bear any costs, so confirm this when the call opens. Run by the EDSAFE AI Alliance; questions to edsafeai@innovateedunyc.org.
  • OpenAI Student Collective, Campus Leads (worldwide) . NOW OPEN, rechecked 23 August 2026: applications for the Fall 2026 cohort run to 31 August 2026 for students in Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Germany and France, and have already closed in the United States, Canada and India. Applications from other countries are accepted for consideration in future cohorts as the programme expands. Campus Leads run AI initiatives on their campus and receive a cash stipend each semester, paid after the semester's activities are completed, plus a ChatGPT subscription and Codex credits for the duration, funding, credits and merchandise for campus events, and the chance of a visit to OpenAI HQ in June 2027. Eligibility: enrolled in an undergraduate programme as of August 2026, expecting to graduate after December 2027, and able to commit 4 to 6 hours a week from August 2026 to June 2027. Kept on the watchlist rather than the desk above because no stipend figure is published and this is a campus-ambassador programme rather than a grant or fellowship. Apply via openai.com/student-collective.
  • Disruption Network Institute Fellowships, round three (Berlin, largely remote) . Round two ran September 2025 to June 2026 on "Investigating the Kill Cloud: AI, Big Tech and Militarisation", covering technological control and repression in war zones, border regions and urban environments, including AI in automated target recognition used to monitor civilians. Findings are presented at the Disruption Network Lab conference in Berlin on 27-29 November 2026, and the next round has historically been announced around September. Rechecked 27 August 2026: the fellows page still lists only the 2023-24 and 2025-26 cohorts with no open call, so re-check from September. Paid fellowships for investigative journalists, researchers, whistleblowers and artists, published through Disruption Network Lab; work is largely remote with the Berlin presentation in person. No stipend figure is published, so ask when the call opens.
  • Nawat Fes Artist Residencies 2027-28 (Fes, Morocco) . The application portal opens December 2026 for a January 2027 deadline (exact date to be announced), covering residencies from October 2027 to July 2028; every slot through July 2027 is already awarded. Two-month residency with free housing in the Fes medina plus a 12,000 MAD (around USD 1,200) stipend, no application or participation fee. Open to all nationalities, with a preference for applicants not already living in Morocco; requires a passport allowing 60+ days visa-free entry and conversational English. Disciplines include visual and performance art, music composition, sound art, film and screenwriting, literature and translation.
  • Wits Innovation Centre Artist-in-Lab Residency (Johannesburg, South Africa) . Last call closed 31 May 2025 and no new cycle is posted; Wits publishes no standing call page, so this links to the last full listing. One of the best-funded art-science residencies on the continent: ZAR 360,000 for nine months (six on-site at the Sydney Brenner Institute for Molecular Bioscience plus three months follow-up), including relocation, medical aid and research costs. Open internationally to practising artists in any discipline with at least a Master's degree. Pairs artists with genomics and other Wits labs.
  • J. Anthony Lukas Work-in-Progress Awards 2027 (Columbia Journalism School and Nieman Foundation) . Submissions reopen in fall 2026; the last cycle closed 4 December 2025. Two annual awards of USD 25,000 each to help complete a book-length work of nonfiction on a topic of American political or social concern (science, tech and media accountability books have won before). Applicants normally need a US publishing contract; check the fall announcement for entry requirements and any submission fee.
  • Allianz Foundation Grants Programme (Europe and the Mediterranean) . The 2025 round closed 10 February 2025 and no 2026 call has been announced; watch for the next cycle, which historically opens around January-February. Grants of EUR 80,000 to 200,000 over up to 24 months for organizations (not individuals) in Europe and the Mediterranean working in Arts and Culture, European Civil Society, or Climate and Environment. The foundation covers up to 75 percent of project costs; at least 25 percent must come from other sources. No application fee.
  • European AI & Society Fund (Europe) . Rechecked 14 August 2026: the fund's Building Narrative Power call (EUR 2m, grants up to EUR 150,000) is open until 31 August 2026 and is already listed on the desk above. The Build and Breakthrough initiatives remain closed to new applicants, and further calls are announced via the fund's newsletter. Pooled fund (Bosch, Mott, Ford, Luminate, Mozilla, Oak, Open Society, Mercator and others) that finances civil society organizations shaping AI in the public interest, through the Build initiative (sustained flexible funding for tech and social justice groups across Europe) and the Breakthrough initiative (EUR 10 million against harmful AI impacts). Organizations only. No application fee.
  • Culture Helps Solidarity (European Cultural Foundation, Creative Europe) . First rounds closed in spring 2026 (Collaboration Grants 31 March, Project Grants 16 April, Individual Care Grants 18 May); more than 20 further rounds follow through March 2028. Over EUR 1.4 million total for cultural organizations, artists and community partners supporting Ukrainian cultural cooperation and displaced people, via Individual Care Grants, Project Grants and Collaboration Grants between Ukrainian and European organizations. No application fee.
  • Bloomberg New Contemporaries 2027 (UK) . The 2026 open call closed 30 March 2026; the next is expected February-March 2027. Flagship UK platform for emerging and early-career artists aged 21+ based in England, Northern Ireland, Scotland or Wales: selected artists join a year-long Artist Development Programme and a touring group exhibition at major venues. Submit up to three works in any medium. Note: GBP 25 non-refundable application fee.
  • Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship 2027-28 . The 2026-27 round closed 14 December 2025; the next call is expected autumn 2026 with a mid-December deadline. Covers 100 percent of tuition plus a USD 45,000 stipend for living, conference and research expenses, with a required 14-week paid summer internship at Bloomberg each fellowship year. For full-time doctoral students in data science, AI and computer science (Ph.D. expected by end of 2029 for the current cycle); apply with CV, two-page research proposal and advisor reference. No visa sponsorship.
  • Bibliothek Andreas Zuest Residency 2027 (Oberegg, Switzerland) . Next call expected October 2026 (for summer 2027 residencies), announced via the library's Instagram and newsletter. Six-week fully funded residency at the Alpenhof: free lodging (private bedroom), free meals on-site, travel costs covered, and a CHF 750/month subsistence allowance on request. Open to international and domestic cultural practitioners across all disciplines (visual arts, literature, new media, music, performance, design, architecture, film, photography, research); duos and collectives up to five people welcome.
  • Ford Foundation JustFilms 2027 . Next call expected spring 2027 (the 2026 open call closed around 10 April). Grants typically USD 25,000-100,000, no application fee. Annual four-week open call for artist-driven, feature-length (50+ min) documentaries intersecting with social justice; open to filmmakers globally, with focus on regions where Ford has offices.
  • WRO Media Art Biennale (Wroclaw, Poland) . The 2026 New Media Week competition closed 30 June 2026; the next WRO open call is expected in 2027 (the biennale runs on a roughly two-year cycle). International competition for professional new-media artists (24+) with projects in new media art: installations, systems and environments, moving image and visual narratives, media performance and live acts, technological objects and media sculptures, and research projects or tool prototypes. Submissions via newmediaweek.com; check the WRO Center site for the next call.
  • U-jazdowski Residencies (Ujazdowski Castle Centre for Contemporary Art, Warsaw) . Open calls are held irregularly and announced on the centre's site and social channels. Residencies for artists and researchers across disciplines (including new media), with recent cycles reflecting on coexistence and the post-human world; stipend, accommodation and studio typically provided. Watch the open-calls page for the next round.
  • Onassis AiR . Next call expected early 2027. Stipend, accommodation, travel and working space for a 10-week residency in Athens; about thirty fellows per cohort across visual arts, performance, sound, art and advanced tech, curatorial and writing.
  • Rupert Residencies (Vilnius, Lithuania) . Open calls are announced irregularly on the Rupert site and newsletter; the ALTERLIFE co-production with Sonic Acts (Vilnius plus Amsterdam) last closed August 2025. Rupert's residencies are fully funded: accommodation, workspace, a stipend and travel support, with production budgets for the resulting work. Interdisciplinary practices incorporating sound, video and research are a strong fit. Watch the residencies page for the next round.
  • Nida Art Colony lens-based residency (Nida, Lithuania) . The Lithuanian Photographers Association x VAA Nida Art Colony call for a one-month residency on the Curonian Spit last closed 1 June 2026 (for May 2027); the next is expected around spring 2027. Funded: a EUR 600 grant, travel up to EUR 300, housing covered, plus up to EUR 300 for printing/digitisation; EUR 20 application fee. For artists working in photography or lens-based media broadly. Note: Nida's separate open-ended individual residency is a paid stay (~EUR 580/month, no stipend), so only this funded lens-based call is tracked here.
  • Tarbell Fellowship 2027 (AI Journalism) . Next call expected late 2026. USD 60,000-80,000 (regular fellows) or USD 90,000-110,000 (senior fellows) for a 12-month placement at major US/UK newsrooms building an AI-coverage beat.
  • GovAI Summer Fellowship 2027 . Next call expected late 2026. Three-month AI-governance fellowship with mentors at the Centre for the Governance of AI; tracks include Research (London), Applied (GBP 12,000) and a DC-based track (USD 21,000 plus London travel support).
  • openDemocracy x Tech Policy Press Tech Reporting Fellowship 2027 . Next call expected late 2026. UK-embedded tech reporting fellowship for journalists (including researchers, lawyers and technologists transitioning into journalism), double-published by openDemocracy and Tech Policy Press. GBP 30,000 per annum over 12 months.
  • Knight Science Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) . Next call expected around 9 January 2027. Nine-month residential fellowship at MIT for journalists with 3+ consecutive years covering science, health, tech or environmental issues. USD 85,000 stipend plus travel, housing and basic health insurance.
  • Reuters Institute Journalist Fellowship 2027-28 (Oxford) . Next call expected January 2027 (for cohorts starting October 2027, January 2028, April 2028). Mid-career residential fellowship at Oxford to study journalism, AI and digital transformation in depth. Fully funded with a stipend for living and travel costs.
  • Nieman Fellowship 2027-28 (Harvard) . Next call opens first week of October 2026; deadlines 1 December 2026 (international) and 31 January 2027 (US). Academic-year fellowship at Harvard with stipend, tuition, housing and health insurance for working journalists pursuing a self-directed project, often in tech/digital culture directions.
  • Andrew Carnegie Fellows 2027 . Nominations expected to open September 2026 and close around early November 2026. USD 200,000 over 1-2 years for US-based scholars, journalists and public intellectuals on a book-length project, usually framed around US political polarisation and cohesion. Institutional nomination required.
  • NEH Public Scholars Program 2027 . Next call expected April 2027. USD 30,000 to USD 60,000 per grant for non-fiction book projects aimed at general audiences. Open to US citizens and permanent residents; independent writers and journalists explicitly encouraged.
  • Heinrich Boell Transatlantic Media Fellowship 2027 . Next call expected around March 2027. Transatlantic reporting stipend for journalists in any medium: USD 4,000 (on-the-ground with travel) or USD 2,000 (digital/virtual fellowship). For US/Canada-based journalists writing on the EU, or German journalists writing on the US/Canada. Distinct from the Foundation's Global Majority AI Fellowship that is already on the desk.
  • Saari Residence 2028 (Kone Foundation, Finland) . Rechecked 14 August 2026: the annual window runs 1 to 31 March, so expect the 2028 call in March 2027 rather than autumn 2026. EUR 2,700-3,800/month (experience-tiered) plus a two-month residency in Mynamaki for international writers, translators, composers, curators and critics. The 2028 cycle has reduced capacity due to renovation.
  • RSL Giles St Aubyn Awards for Non-Fiction 2027 . Next call expected September 2026. GBP 10,000 / 5,000 / 2,500 across three tiered awards for UK or Ireland-based first-time nonfiction writers with a contract for their first commissioned book.
  • Robert B. Silvers Foundation Grants for Work in Progress 2027 . Next call expected around March 2027. Up to USD 10,000 for long-form critics and essayists worldwide working on literary or arts criticism, intellectual essay, political analysis or social reportage. Must have a publishing agreement.
  • Berton House Writers' Residency 2027 (Writers' Trust of Canada) . Next call expected around March 2027. Two months housing, travel covered and CAD 4,000 stipend at Pierre Berton's childhood home in Dawson City, Yukon for writers in poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, playwriting or children's literature. Verify international eligibility (some years have been Canadian-only).
  • PEN Translates 2027 (English PEN) . Next round expected November 2026 or May 2027 (biannual). Funds UK publishers (and global publishers via PEN Translates x SALT) for up to 75% of literary translation costs into English, 100% for small publishers; the translator is paid by the publisher. Distinct from the PEN America PEN/Heim Translation Fund already on the desk.
  • Tejumola Olaniyan Creative Writers Fellowship 2027 (The Africa Institute, Sharjah) . Next call expected early 2027. AED 50,000 (approximately USD 13,600) residency fellowship at The Africa Institute in Sharjah for writers from Africa and its diaspora engaging with Africa and African diaspora themes. Any genre.
  • Mophradat Writing Sabbaticals 2026-27 . Next round expected late 2026 (biannual). Sabbatical stipend (amount varies) plus peer editor support for published Arab fiction writers based in the Arab world finalising a manuscript. Priority for those writing in Arabic.
  • Goethe-Institut Documenta Fellowship 2027 . Next call expected around January 2027. EUR 2,000/month for six months plus visa, housing and travel support for a research fellowship at the documenta archive in Kassel; open to non-German-resident writers, scholars and curators researching contemporary art and documenta. German C1 ideally required.
  • Commonwealth Short Story Prize 2027 . Opens 1 September 2026; deadline typically early November 2026. GBP 5,000 to overall winner; GBP 2,500 to regional winners. International short story prize for Commonwealth citizens aged 18+; translations welcome. Free entry.
  • Akademie Schloss Solitude TEXTUAL Fellowship 2028-30 . Next call expected autumn 2027 (triennial cycle, for 2028-30 fellowships). EUR 1,300+/month stipend plus housing and travel for 6 or 9 months in Stuttgart; for early-to-mid-career international writers in literature, translation and dramatic writing (under the "TEXTUAL" sphere). Eligibility window: 2-10 years of independent practice after training.
  • Stage IX Residency (NXT Museum, Amsterdam) . Next call expected late 2026 or early 2027. Practice-based 8-10 month residency at NXT Museum (the Netherlands' first museum dedicated to art-tech-science-sound). Emerging track: EUR 18,000 artist fee plus EUR 5,000 R&D; Established track: EUR 26,000 plus EUR 15,000. Practice areas include spatial sound, VR/XR/AR, gamified/interactive media, kinetic and light-based installation, scenography and immersive theatre.
  • Mesh Festival 2026/27 (HEK Basel) . Next call expected Q4 2026 for the 2027 edition. Co-organised by HEK Basel, HGK Basel FHNW and iart ag - a festival presenting experimental art-tech projects in Basel and Muenchenstein. Selected projects are presented at the October festival; verify the fee/commission structure in the next round announcement.
  • ZKM Rauschenberg Residencies 2027/28 (Karlsruhe) . Next call expected early 2027. Three-month residency at ZKM Karlsruhe (with the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation) for artists bridging performative art and creative technology. EUR 4,000 scholarship plus EUR 1,000 travel, accommodation and up to EUR 2,500 materials budget.
  • Harvestworks 2027 Artists-in-Residence (NYC) . Next call expected late 2026. Year-long NYC residency at the Harvestworks T.E.A.M. Lab for US-based artists making interactive, audio/video, AR/VR or ML-based work, with an assigned engineer. The 2027 stipend is not yet confirmed - verify before applying.
  • FACT Digital Artist Residencies 2027 (Liverpool) . Next call expected early 2027. GBP 4,500 per resident plus Unreal Engine training and curatorial/creative mentoring. 18-week paid residency for early-career artists living in North West England or North Wales, in partnership with Lucid Games, Homotopia and DaDa.
  • Michigan Central x Newlab Fellows-in-Residence 2027 (Detroit) . Next call expected early 2027. USD 30,000 unrestricted plus fabrication facilities, research access and mentorship for a 12-week Detroit-based residency at the intersection of art, technology and society. Practice areas include data visualisation, wearable tech, accessibility, sustainability and art + health tech.
  • ZER01NE Creator Open Call 2027 (Hyundai, Seoul) . Rechecked 27 August 2026: no 2027 call is posted yet. The 2026 Creator open call went live in October 2025, so expect the 2027 call around October 2026 and re-check from then. Note the site blocks some automated checks, so confirm on ZER01NE's own channels. Hyundai Motor Group's annual open call for art/tech creators; selected projects receive financial support, mentorship and a showcase at ZER01NE Day in Seoul each October. Themes: AI, climate tech, robotics and future mobility.
  • Creative Capital Award 2028 (US) . Next call expected around April 2027. Up to USD 50,000 unrestricted project grant (Creative Capital Award) plus USD 10,000 State of the Art Prize. Major US unrestricted artist grant with a dedicated "Technology" discipline plus multidisciplinary and socially engaged forms; open to US-based artists in all 50 states and territories.
  • Somerset House Studios x UNESCO AI Ethics Residency . Next round expected around early 2027 (the last call closed 15 January 2026). GBP 7,500 artist fee plus GBP 7,500 production budget for a London residency on the ethics of AI; the previous round was open internationally. Somerset House's other programmes (Creative Technologies Fellowship, n-Space) recur on the same page.
  • Berkman Klein Center Fellowships 2027-28 (Harvard) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the annual call is confirmed closed ("we are no longer accepting applications") with no reopening date announced; next call still expected autumn 2026 (last deadline was 5 December), and the Center also runs one-off fellowship calls at any point in the year, announced via its newsletter. Stipends up to USD 75,000 per year for fellows working on AI and society, privacy, and digital rights; open internationally, practitioners and artists included.
  • Chaos Communication Congress: Art & Installations (Hamburg) . Call for participation historically opens late September with a late-October deadline for the December Congress. Unpaid exhibition slot, but a flagship venue for counter-surveillance and critical tech art.
  • HollyShorts Film Festival 2027 (Los Angeles) . NOW OPEN, rechecked 27 August 2026: submissions for the 22nd edition are live on FilmFreeway, with the earlybird deadline 6 November 2026 and the regular deadline 8 January 2027. Oscar-qualifying shorts festival at the TCL Chinese Theatres, with 25-plus award categories including Best Short, Best Live Action, Best Animation and Best Documentary (all Academy-qualifying), plus automatic distribution on Bitpix for selected films. International. Kept on the watchlist rather than the desk above because entry is paid (fees typically USD 45-90 by tier) and no cash prize figure is published.
  • IndieCade 2027 (Los Angeles) . Submissions expected to open around February-March 2027 (the 2026 cycle closed 15 June). International festival of independent games and interactive media, including experimental and installation-based work; fees approx. USD 80-135.
  • Feminist Center for Creative Work: Artist in Residence (LA) . Next call expected late 2026 (last closed 30 November 2025). Project residencies supporting feminist creative practice; prioritizes artists who can be consistently in Los Angeles; free to apply.
  • City of LA COLA-IMAP Fellowship 2027-28 (LA residents only) . FY2027-28 cycle expected to open late September 2026 with an end-of-October deadline. Historically USD 10,000 for mid-career City of Los Angeles artists to premiere a new solo work; LA residents only.
  • Digital Arts Studios Belfast: Home Residency . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the page still shows only the closed call for the August to November 2026 period (deadline was 8 July 2026). Open calls run three times a year for April-July, August-November and December-March periods, so the next cycle (December 2026 to March 2027) call is expected around autumn 2026. Four-month digital art residency with studio access and support; aimed at artists based in Ireland or the UK; free to apply.
  • Cove Park Awarded Residencies (Scotland) . Rechecked 27 August 2026: Cove Park still states the next general call is expected autumn 2026, covering fully funded residencies (fees, travel, accommodation) of two weeks to three months taking place April 2027 to December 2028; eligibility strands vary by funder, some international.
  • Thunderbird Drone Festival (Oklahoma State University-Tulsa) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the official OSU site still displays the 2025 edition (entries by 25 August, nominees 17 September, awards show 10 October) with no 2026 call, so treat the festival as possibly dormant and confirm with OSU-Tulsa before relying on it. Drone film and photo competition with awards. Use the official OSU page only; the festival's old .com domain appears hijacked.
  • Drone Film Festival Poland (Wroclaw) . The 2026 call typically opens in autumn for the December festival. Crystal Drone awards across six categories including AI and FPV; international.
  • Surveillance Studies Network Arts Prize . Biennial arts prize for work engaging with surveillance; next edition expected 2027-28. The affiliated journal Surveillance & Society also accepts artist contributions on a rolling basis via its arts editor.
  • Bertha Artivism Awards 2027 . Applications open August 2026 (closing date not yet published; cohort starts January 2027). Up to USD 20,000 for a one-year activist-art project made with a social justice organization, campaign, or movement; individuals and collectives worldwide; free to apply.
  • FILE 2027: Electronic Language International Festival (Sao Paulo) . Next call expected around December 2026 to February 2027 (the 2026 call closed 19 February). Latin America's leading electronic/media art festival, free to enter, international, with an explicit AI-art axis.
  • CIFO x Ars Electronica Awards 2027 (Latin American artists only) . Rechecked 27 August 2026: still no 2027 call announced and no date given, so keep watching. Next call expected mid to late 2026 (2026 winners were announced December 2025). USD 45,000 total across awardees plus exhibition at Ars Electronica Linz; Latin American media artists only.
  • FICG 42: Guadalajara International Film Festival . Submissions expected September to December 2026 for the April 2027 festival. One of Latin America's most important festivals; primarily Ibero-American competition focus, check category eligibility.
  • FICCI 66: Cartagena International Film Festival . The FICCI 66 call should open in the second half of 2026 with a deadline around December (FICCI 65 closed 8 December 2025). Latin America's oldest film festival; the previous cycle offered a USD 100,000 prize pool.
  • Radio Tsonami / Tsonami Sound Art Festival (Valparaiso) . The Radio Tsonami broadcast open call (international, radio and sound works) should recur around October 2026; residency calls for the XX-anniversary festival (November 2027) closed June 2026.
  • Pivo Research Residency 2027 (Sao Paulo) . Next call expected around March 2027. Free, internationally open research residency in the Copan building with curatorial and institutional support; Pivo Salvador's separate Brazil-prioritized call recurs around October-November.
  • Chinati Foundation Artist in Residence (Marfa) . Next open call: January 2027 for the 2028-2029 cohorts. Two-month residency with an apartment at the museum, a downtown studio, and USD 4,000 for honorarium, travel, and materials; open internationally, all media.
  • BFI Flare 2027: London LGBTQIA+ Film Festival (40th edition) . The 2027 call is expected to open in autumn 2026 with a deadline around early December (the 2026 call closed 5 December 2025). Europe's flagship queer film festival; shorts, mid-length, and features; fees historically low or none.
  • Roze Filmdagen 2027: 30th Amsterdam LGBTQ+ Film Festival . Expect a deadline around 1 December 2026 (the 29th edition closed 1 December 2025; the FilmFreeway page for the 30th already exists). Fiction and documentary competitions with prizes; historically free to submit; festival 10-21 March 2027.
  • Fire Island Artist Residency 2027 . The 2027 call is expected to open early 2027 with a deadline around 1 April. Summer residency exclusively for LGBTQ+ visual artists: housing plus an intensive visiting-critic program; historically open to non-US applicants; modest application fee (~USD 25).
  • Zinegoak 2027: Bilbao LGTBIQA+ Film and Performing Arts Festival . The new call is expected to open around mid-October 2026. International submissions; screening and awards at the Basque Country's queer film and performing arts festival.
  • Berlinale 2027 film submissions . The submission portal for the 77th Berlin International Film Festival (10-21 February 2027) opens in September 2026; deadlines 21 October 2026 (features, 60 min+) and 4 November 2026 (shorts, up to 30 min). Open internationally; entry fee applies (2027 amounts not yet published; recent editions charged roughly EUR 85-190 for features and EUR 30-85 for shorts).
  • DAAD Artists-in-Berlin Program 2028 (Berliner Kuenstlerprogramm) . Applications historically open mid-October to November with a deadline around 15 December; expect the call for 2028 residencies in late 2026. Fully funded ~12-month Berlin residency: monthly grant covering living costs plus apartment/workspace support and travel. Open application ONLY in film, literature, and music and sound (visual arts is nomination-only); open to artists not resident in Germany; no fee.
  • A MAZE. / Berlin 2027 (16th International Games and Playful Media Festival) . Award submissions for the 2026 edition opened in autumn with early bird until the end of the year; expect the 2027 call on a similar schedule. Festival exhibition plus award categories (Most Amazing, Human Human Machine, Digital Moment) for games, XR, alt-controllers, interactive installations and AI works; international; submission fee around EUR 50 (EUR 35 early bird, pay-what-you-want supporter option).

Funded mentorship with an international mentor plus festival presentation at Radialsystem Berlin; open internationally across disciplines including sound, digital culture and transmedia practices.
  • Harun Farocki Institut Residency 2027 (Berlin) . Annual call; the 2026 round was published in early February with a spring deadline, so expect the 2027 call around January-February 2027. Three-month funded Berlin residency for film and media artists working in essayistic, documentary and research-based practices; open internationally.
  • Schloss Wiepersdorf fellowships 2028 (Brandenburg) . The 2027 call closed 15 April 2026; the next application window is expected 15 February to 15 April 2027. Residential fellowships near Berlin: EUR 1,200 per month plus room and board plus EUR 480 materials allowance; open internationally across literature, visual arts, composition and cultural research.
  • HTW Berlin IUNO Artistic Fellowship (AI + XR) . The 2026 deadline passed 31 March and required being Berlin-based; a 2027 round is not yet confirmed, so treat this as speculative. EU-funded fellowship at HTW Berlin for artistic work with AI and extended reality; extremely on-profile if a new round opens and if Berlin-based at the time.
  • Salt Artistic Research and Production Grant (Istanbul, Turkey) . EUR 20,000 per project, run by Salt with the BBVA Foundation, for artists and researchers from Turkiye investigating contemporary social questions across art, architecture, design, and social and urban studies. Interdisciplinary and research-led practices are the explicit target, which makes this the closest fit on the desk's profile of anything in Turkey.

Two five-month residencies in Berlin for visual artists whose main home and studio is Istanbul: EUR 2,000 per month covering travel, materials and living costs, plus a rent-free studio apartment at Kunstquartier Bethanien in Kreuzberg. Run with the Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, nGbK and Kunstquartier Bethanien. Students enrolled at a university are excluded; basic English or German required; portfolio capped at 10 pages; applications in Turkish or English.

Six-month programme for visual artists from Turkiye at SAHA's IMC venues: a personal workspace, an honorarium and a production budget. SAHA has supported over 650 artists, curators, writers and art initiatives since 2011.
  • CultureCIVIC (Goethe-Institut Istanbul, EU-funded, Turkey) . All five 2026 rounds have closed (Art Production 13 January, Grassroots Projects 10 March, Inter-City Networking 14 April, Structural Support extended to 16 June), and Grassroots runs twice a year, so another call is due. EU project managed by Goethe-Institut Istanbul for civil society organisations, artists, initiatives and activists working in culture and arts in Turkiye. Four lines: Grassroots Projects; Structural Support up to EUR 20,000 per organisation; Inter-City Networking for civil society organisations with legal status; and Art Production, up to EUR 6,000 in the most recent round, for visual artists aged 25-45 including sound, video, installation and interdisciplinary work.
  • SaDe Artist Support Fund (IKSV, Turkey) . The 2026 round closed 30 March; the fund is annual, so expect the next call around February-March 2027. Five awards of EUR 5,000 each for artists under 35 producing in visual arts: painting, sculpture, ceramics, photography, glass, illustration, drawing or printmaking. Distinct from the IKSV Young Artist Fund travel grant already on the desk.
  • Gate 27 Residency 2027 (Istanbul and Ayvalik, Turkey) . Rechecked 23 August 2026: the official page confirms the 2026 programme is filled and states that the application process for the 2027 residency programme is planned to begin in the fall of 2026. Four to twelve weeks in Yenikoy, Istanbul, or four weeks in Ayvalik, with no application or accommodation fee: private room and bathroom, studio access, weekly grocery shopping in Istanbul or three meals a day in Ayvalik, and a 300 TL weekly public transport card. Open to visual arts, curation, literature, music, architecture and design. Caveat against the desk's paid-only bar: Gate 27 covers no travel, visa or production costs, so it is free to attend rather than funded.
  • Braid Arts and Culture Fund (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania) . No open round is posted and calls are announced by TICAH rather than on a fixed schedule; the inaugural cohort supported 23 projects. Grants of up to KES 700,000 from the Trust for Indigenous Culture and Health with the British Council's Cultural Heritage for Inclusive Growth programme, for artists, cultural practitioners, organisations, businesses, collectives and cultural centres across East Africa, bridging traditional heritage and contemporary practice.
  • Africa No Filter grants (Africa and diaspora) . Applications are call-based rather than rolling and nothing is open right now. Grants for storytellers whose work focuses on Africa and the diaspora: Project Support up to USD 10,000, Operational and Capacity Building up to USD 15,000, Kekere Storytellers Fund USD 500-3,000, and Last Mile Film Fund up to USD 10,000 for features or USD 5,000 for shorts, with an overall USD 25,000 ceiling. Individuals and registered organisations both eligible, and applicants can be based anywhere as long as the project focuses on Africa. Important: joining the African Narrative Collective is mandatory before you can apply, so register in advance rather than when a call opens.
  • Docubox, the East African Documentary Film Fund (Nairobi, Kenya) . Docubox says its own funding cycle is irregular, some years three or four calls and some years none, and calls go out by newsletter and social media rather than being posted on the site, so subscribe rather than watching the page. Its first fiction feature development lab closed 24 May 2026 and awarded USD 5,000 development grants to five Kenyan projects out of seven producers taken into a five-day lab.
  • Mozilla Tech and Society Fellowship 2027 . The 2026 nominations round has closed; the call has opened in December in past cycles. USD 125,000 for Independent Fellows (USD 100,000 stipend plus USD 25,000 project budget) or USD 100,000 for Embedded Fellows (USD 75,000 plus USD 25,000), for technologists, researchers, advocates and creators building a more just, open and equitable internet. Launched with the Ford Foundation. Relevant to Kenya coverage: Embedded Fellows must be located in Kenya, South Africa, Brazil, the MENA region, Mexico, the UK, the US or the EU. Both self-nominations and third-party nominations accepted.

Filed Away (for 1 year)

Frequently asked questions

What kinds of grants are listed on The Grant Desk?

Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies for artists, researchers and technologists. Categories cover AI and AI safety, digital and mixed-media arts, film and video, research and journalism, tech and infrastructure, and cross-disciplinary or social-impact work. Almost every entry is funded; pure "exposure only" calls and pay-to-play submission fees are generally filtered out, though a few notable unpaid open calls and festival submissions are included as clearly flagged exceptions.

How often is the list updated?

A chronically online human finds candidates by hand from newsletters, Slack and Discord channels, Bluesky, RSS feeds and grant-maker pages, then curates the strong fits. Updates happen periodically rather than on a fixed schedule. Closed calls are auto-filed away after their deadline, so the visible list stays current.

Why are some times of year quieter on the desk?

Funding has seasons. Most big annual cycles close in late autumn or in March and April, with the next wave of restocking typically landing in autumn for January cycles. Mid-spring to early summer tends to be a "dead zone" for new openings, so if the desk looks quiet then, that is usually the funding calendar rather than the desk going stale.

Can I subscribe by RSS or add deadlines to my calendar?

Yes. There is an RSS feed and an ICS calendar feed for every region and category combination. Subscribe in your reader (Feedly, NetNewsWire, etc.) or add the calendar to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook so deadlines reach you wherever you already read.

Can I export grants to feed into an LLM?

Yes. The "Export for LLM" button in the shortlist bar exports either your shortlist or whatever the current filters are showing. Markdown is the recommended format for pasting into a chat: one heading per opportunity with labelled fields, plus a header line recording which filters were applied. JSON is there for sorting or scoring entries programmatically, and CSV for spreadsheets. "Summary only" trims each description to its opening paragraph if the full export is too large for the context window. The file is generated in your browser, so nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Who runs The Grant Desk, and how can I suggest a grant?

The Grant Desk is maintained by Artificial Nouveau Studio. To suggest a grant, use the "Suggest a grant" form in the top strip; if it is paid and a strong fit, it lands on the desk.
